page: Amazon Web Services a1.large is an ARM-based virtual machine powered by the first-generation AWS Graviton processor. Built on the AWS Nitro System hypervisor, this instance features 2 dedicated vCPUs utilizing the ARMv8 Cortex-A72 architecture running at 2.3 GHz. It is equipped with 4.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 2.0 GB per core. The processor includes 32 KB of L1d cache and 2 MB of L2 cache, with no L3 cache. There is no local storage or GPU hardware bundled with this instance type.

Performance benchmarks indicate that the a1.large is positioned at the lower end of the compute spectrum. While stress-ng single-core CPU performance registers in the average tier at 1489.88, multi-core performance drops to the bottom 25% with a score of 2934.26. Memory bandwidth benchmarks, including read-only and write tests on large blocks, fall into the bottom 10%, as do Geekbench and Passmark CPU scores. Static web serving throughput is measured at 0.61 GB/sec, and small-model LLM inference speeds are limited to 5.35 tokens/sec for text generation.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the a1.large offers a low-cost entry point into ARM64 development and testing. Because it utilizes dedicated physical cores without hyperthreading, it provides predictable execution for lightweight workloads despite its modest performance profile. It is best suited for basic web serving, containerized microservices, ARM-native software compilation, and development environments that do not require high memory bandwidth or intensive floating-point calculations.
description: Amazon Web Services a1.large is an ARM64-based instance powered by the first-generation AWS Graviton processor with a Cortex-A72 microarchitecture. Operating at 2.3 GHz, it features 2 dedicated physical cores, 4.0 GB of system memory, and a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps. The instance runs on the AWS Nitro System hypervisor and does not include local storage or GPU accelerators. Benchmark data places its performance in the lower tiers, with average single-core stress-ng results but weak multi-core and memory bandwidth metrics. This instance offers a cost-effective platform for ARM-native development, testing, and lightweight, scale-out applications. It is best suited for basic web serving, containerized microservices, and software compilation tasks that benefit from dedicated physical cores without requiring high memory throughput or advanced vector instructions.
